data.name: Coffea Eugenioides Finca Inmaculada Filter
data.story:
Rarity is not simply a matter of limited production; it's often the result of generations of careful preservation.

As one of the original parent species of Arabica, Coffea Eugenioides has remained largely absent from commercial cultivation because of its naturally low yields and delicate growing requirements.

At Finca Inmaculada, this rare species is cultivated with exceptional care, representing the farm's ongoing pursuit of coffee diversity, innovation, and preservation.
data.tastingNotes: Stevia, Orange Candy, Passion Fruit, Papaya, Strawberry

data.name: Gayo Anaerobic Natural 300h
data.tagline: Deep Gayo intensity with a long, lingering, fruity finish.
data.story:
Gayo coffee comes from the highlands of Bener Meriah in Aceh, northern Sumatra — one of Indonesia's most respected Arabica-producing regions. The Gayo Highlands' cool climate, mist-covered mornings, and volcanic soils slow cherry maturation, allowing sugars and organic acids to develop evenly within the beans.

Among Indonesia's most distinguished highland Arabicas, Gayo coffee is celebrated for its balance, clarity, and layered flavor structure — combining Indonesian depth with brighter acidity than most Sumatran origins.
data.reason: This 300-hour anaerobic natural pushes Gayo's fermentation to its limits — berries, concord grapes, red apples, and dates with a deep, lingering finish. We chose it for its intense, fruit-driven profile that showcases what extended anaerobic processing can unlock in Gayo's highland beans.
data.tastingNotes: Berries, Concord Grapes, Red Apples, Dates

data.name: Gayo Bener Meriah 3D Washed
data.story: Inspired by a layered approach to post-harvest processing, this 3D Washed lot undergoes successive stages of anaerobic natural and honey fermentation before a final washed finish. The result is a process that embraces innovation while preserving the character of Gayo's Bener Meriah Highlands.

data.name: Java Ijen Full Washed
data.story:
Java Ijen coffee is grown on the mineral-rich volcanic soils of the Ijen Plateau in East Java, across estates in Pancor, Jampit, and Belawan at 1,400–1,600 masl. The Ijen region was among the first in Indonesia to produce Arabica, with a coffee history dating back to the Dutch colonial era. In 2013, Arabika Ijen Raung became the first East Java Arabica to receive a patent for high quality, and the region is pursuing Geographical Indication certification alongside prestigious Indonesian coffees like Toraja and Mandheling.

The combination of volcanic altitude, cool temperatures, and the plateau's unique microclimate produces coffees with a distinctive Java character — clean, balanced, and subtly complex.
data.reason: This full washed Java Ijen delivers apple, lemon juice, brown sugar, and chocolate milk — a clean, approachable profile that represents the best of Java's historic coffee tradition. We chose it as our staple Indonesian washed coffee because Ijen's volcanic terroir produces a reliable, high-quality cup with the kind of balanced sweetness that works in any brew method.
data.tastingNotes: Apple, Lemon Juice, Brown Sugar, Chocolate Milk

data.name: Kerinci Blueberry Infused
data.story:
Kerinci coffee is produced in the Kayu Aro highlands of Jambi province on Sumatra, at 1,400–1,500 masl in the shadow of Mount Kerinci — Sumatra's highest volcano at 3,805 meters. The region lies at the gateway to Kerinci Seblat National Park, where fertile volcanic soil, high altitude, and cool temperatures produce Arabica with bright acidity, floral notes, and complex sweetness.

Kerinci has built a strong reputation in the specialty market, with an association of over 680 producers cultivating coffee on smallholder parcels around the valley's edge.
data.reason: This blueberry co-ferment delivers blueberry and blackcurrant — a bold, fruit-forward profile created through natural anaerobic processing with blueberry infusion using Kerinci highland beans.
